name: How do Colorado’s seasonal climate changes affect baseboard installation?

mainEntity.name: How do Colorado’s seasonal climate changes affect baseboard installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry climates and seasonal humidity swings across the Denver metro area cause framing lumber and subfloors to expand during summer and contract during dry winters. For baseboard work, trim materials must acclimate to indoor conditions before installation to minimize shrinking seams later. Inside corners should be coped rather than simple mitered joints; coped joints remain tight and disguise movement as wall studs shift across dry and humid cycles. Flexible, paintable caulk along top edges also prevents cracks as drywall and framing move.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver’s dry climate causes wood movement, so boards must acclimate indoors. Finish carpenters use coped inside joints and flexible caulk to prevent open seams.
